turns: If a thief uses my debit card and I tell the bank within two days, what's the most I can lose?
reference: 1005.6(b)(1): the lesser of $50 or the unauthorized transfers before notice, if notice is given within two business days of learning of the loss or theft.

turns: What do I need to include when I report an error to the bank?
reference: 1005.11(b)(1): enough to identify the consumer's name and account number, why the consumer believes there is an error, and to the extent possible the type, date and amount; received within 60 days after the statement showing the error was sent.

turns: Is provisional credit due within 10 calendar days?
reference: No: within 10 business days of receiving the notice of error (1005.11(c)(2)(i)), not calendar days.

turns: For a point-of-sale debit card purchase, how long can the bank take to investigate my error report?
reference: Up to 90 days (instead of 45) for point-of-sale debit card transactions, with provisional credit within 10 business days (1005.11(c)(3)(ii)).

turns: Does the bank have to explain its decision if it finds no error?
reference: Yes: 1005.11(d)(1): a written explanation of its findings, and notice that the consumer may request the documents it relied on.
